title: The Transfiguration and True Greatness

questions.question: Which three disciples did Jesus take with Him up a high mountain where He was transfigured?
options: Peter, James, and John
Peter, Andrew, and Philip
John, James, and Judas
Thomas, Matthew, and Peter
questions.explanation: Mark 9:2 (ESV): "And after six days Jesus took with him Peter and James and John, and led them up a high mountain by themselves."

questions.question: During His transfiguration, how are His clothes described?
options: Radiant, intensely white, as no one on earth could bleach them
Like flames of fire dancing rapidly
Gleaming like polished bronze
As transparent as glass
questions.correctAnswer: Radiant, intensely white, as no one on earth could bleach them
questions.explanation: Mark 9:3 (ESV): "and his clothes became radiant, intensely white, as no one on earth could bleach them."

questions.question: Who appeared and was talking with Jesus on the mountain?
options: Elijah with Moses
David and Abraham
Enoch and Noah
Isaiah and Jeremiah
questions.explanation: Mark 9:4 (ESV): "And there appeared to them Elijah with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus."

questions.question: What came addressing them from a cloud that overshadowed them?
options: A voice saying, "This is my beloved Son; listen to him."
Thunder that shook the mountain
A choir of angels singing "Holy!"
A great rushing wind without words
questions.correctAnswer: A voice saying, "This is my beloved Son; listen to him."
questions.explanation: Mark 9:7 (ESV): "And a cloud overshadowed them, and a voice came out of the cloud, 'This is my beloved Son; listen to him.'"

questions.question: Who did Jesus confirm had already come, suffering much as it was written of him, when the disciples asked about Elijah coming first?
options: Elijah has indeed come (referring to John the Baptist)
He was referring to Himself in spirit
He was referring to Peter's ministry later on
He said the scribes were lying about Elijah returning
questions.correctAnswer: Elijah has indeed come (referring to John the Baptist)
questions.explanation: Mark 9:13 (ESV): "But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they pleased, as it is written of him." (Referencing John the Baptist).

questions.question: Coming down the mountain, they found the other disciples arguing with scribes. A man in the crowd brought his son to Jesus because he had a spirit that made him what?
options: Mute (and it would seize him, dash him down, froth, and grind his teeth)
Legless and unable to walk
Covered in terrible sores from head to foot
Constantly reciting blasphemies aloud
questions.correctAnswer: Mute (and it would seize him, dash him down, froth, and grind his teeth)
questions.explanation: Mark 9:17-18 (ESV): "...'Teacher, I brought my son to you, for he has a spirit that makes him mute. And whenever it seizes him, it dashes him down...'"

questions.question: When the father begged Jesus "if you can do anything, have compassion on us," how did Jesus reply about "if you can"?
options: "All things are possible for one who believes."
"I can do anything the Father allows."
"If your faith is perfect, I can cure him."
"Only God can cure this sort."
questions.correctAnswer: "All things are possible for one who believes."
questions.explanation: Mark 9:23 (ESV): "And Jesus said to him, 'If you can! All things are possible for one who believes.'"

questions.question: What did the father of the child cry out immediately after Jesus said this?
options: "I believe; help my unbelief!"
"Lord, give me faith to match yours!"
"Praise be to God who sent you!"
"Forgive my lack of trust from my youth!"
questions.explanation: Mark 9:24 (ESV): "Immediately the father of the child cried out and said, 'I believe; help my unbelief!'"

questions.question: When the disciples asked Jesus privately why they could not cast it out, what reason did Jesus give?
options: "This kind cannot be driven out by anything but prayer." (some manuscripts add "and fasting")
"Because you were afraid of the crowd."
"Your authority is limited to minor spirits."
"The boy was not truly willing to be healed."
questions.correctAnswer: "This kind cannot be driven out by anything but prayer." (some manuscripts add "and fasting")
questions.explanation: Mark 9:29 (ESV): "And he said to them, 'This kind cannot be driven out by anything but prayer.'"

questions.question: On their way to Capernaum, what were the disciples arguing about with one another on the road?
options: About who was the greatest
About who would pay the tax at the gate
About what Jesus meant by rising from the dead
About who should betray Him
questions.explanation: Mark 9:34 (ESV): "But they kept silent, for on the way they had argued with one another about who was the greatest."

questions.question: Jesus told the twelve: "If anyone would be first, he must be..." what?
options: "last of all and servant of all."
"the one who gives all he owns to the poor."
"willing to suffer before the Sanhedrin."
"the bravest in battle."
questions.correctAnswer: "last of all and servant of all."
questions.explanation: Mark 9:35 (ESV): "And he sat down and called the twelve. And he said to them, 'If anyone would be first, he must be last of all and servant of all.'"

questions.question: John told Jesus they tried to stop a man casting out demons in Jesus' name because he was not following them. What did Jesus say?
options: "Do not stop him, for no one who does a mighty work in my name will be able soon afterward to speak evil of me."
"You did well, for there are false teachers everywhere."
"Bring him to me that I may test him."
"Let his own synagogue judge him."
questions.correctAnswer: "Do not stop him, for no one who does a mighty work in my name will be able soon afterward to speak evil of me."
questions.explanation: Mark 9:39 (ESV): "But Jesus said, 'Do not stop him, for no one who does a mighty work in my name will be able soon afterward to speak evil of me.'"

questions.question: Jesus said if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Him to sin, it would be better for him to have what?
options: A great millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea
His tongue cut from his mouth
To be blinded by hot irons
To be scourged forty times minus one
questions.correctAnswer: A great millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea
questions.explanation: Mark 9:42 (ESV): "Whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to sin, it would be better for him if a great millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea."

questions.question: If your hand causes you to sin, what does Jesus hyperbolically say you should do, because it is better to enter life crippled than go to hell with two hands?
options: Cut it off
Tie it down
Wash it in bitter water
Strike it with a rod
questions.explanation: Mark 9:43 (ESV): "And if your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life crippled than with two hands to go to hell, to the unquenchable fire."

questions.question: How does Jesus describe hell concerning the "worm" and the "fire"?
options: "Where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched."
"Where the fire burns only the wicked temporarily."
"Where the worm eats the soul and fire consumes the mind."
"Where there is weeping but no flame."
questions.correctAnswer: "Where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched."
questions.explanation: Mark 9:48 (ESV): "'where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.'"

key_verse_text: And Jesus said to him, "'If you can'! All things are possible for one who believes."
